accept: One lesson: cutting, answered by lever and wedge, in either order. Both are required.
The cutting lesson may be the first mechanism with no gap, or come second after a blade given, with a gap.
The finger loops and grips are givens. The rivet is part of the cutting lesson or a given.
linkage is bent here. A third sub-function about holding the blades together is questionable, not wrong, if its primitive is honest.

plan.job: Cuts paper along a line with one squeeze of the hand.
uses: Open the blades round the paper.

mechanisms.name: Crossing blades
mechanisms.does: Cuts paper between two blades that slide past each other.

subfunctions.does: Press on the paper along a thin line
Squeeze harder than fingers can alone

mechanisms.name: Finger loops
mechanisms.does: Give the thumb and fingers a comfortable hold.
